title: GitHub Actions workflow inline script injection via unquoted user inputs
description: Dex2cWorkflowGenerator directly embeds unquoted github.event.inputs expressions into bash run scripts in dex2c.yml, allowing malicious workflow parameters to execute arbitrary shell commands and steal repository signing secrets.
root_cause: Dex2cWorkflowGenerator.kt string template interpolates ${{ github.event.inputs.* }} directly inside run: | scripts rather than passing them via intermediate environment variables.
intended_behavior: Workflow inputs should be mapped to environment variables (e.g., env: APP_NAME: ${{ github.event.inputs.app_name }}) and referenced via safe shell variables ($APP_NAME).

trace.description: Workflow defines workflow_dispatch inputs including apk_path, apk_url, app_name, custom_loader.
Unvalidated curl and cp commands directly embed ${{ github.event.inputs.apk_url }} and ${{ github.event.inputs.apk_path }}.
Raw string interpolation of ${{ github.event.inputs.app_name }} and ${{ github.event.inputs.apk_path }} in step sharing signing secrets (KEYSTORE_B64, KEYSTORE_PASS).

evidence.description: APP_NAME="${{ github.event.inputs.app_name }}" evaluated directly in bash script with repository secrets present.

conditions.description: Workflow is dispatched with custom input containing shell metacharacters.

execution.attacker_perspective: A user or CI dispatcher triggering the GitHub Actions workflow with crafted inputs.
instructions: Trigger workflow dispatch with malicious app_name or apk_path.
execution.observed_result: Bash command injection in runner step with access to KEYSTORE_BASE64 and keystore passwords.

remediation.strategy: Pass all github.event.inputs through env: blocks in the action step rather than inline string interpolation.

likelihood.reason: Requires workflow dispatch permissions or access to dispatch the generated workflow.

impact.reason: Arbitrary command execution in GitHub Actions runner and exfiltration of production signing keystore secrets.

confidence.reason: Direct code review of generated workflow YAML confirms lack of environment variable binding.

title: Insecure fallback to static hardcoded AES key on AndroidKeyStore exception
description: KeystoreTokenEncryptor catches all Exceptions when acquiring the AndroidKeyStore key or performing cryptographic operations, and silently falls back to a deterministic, hardcoded static byte array for AES-GCM encryption of GitHub personal access tokens.
root_cause: KeystoreTokenEncryptor.kt uses a hardcoded 32-byte static fallbackKey on any Exception, compromising confidentiality of OAuth tokens whenever KeyStore is locked, uninitialized, or fails.
intended_behavior: Cryptographic operations on sensitive OAuth credentials should fail closed with an explicit error to the user rather than silently encrypting credentials with a publicly derived static key.

trace.description: User enters or refreshes GitHub OAuth access token.
Catch-all blocks catch Exception and return fallbackKey.
Cipher initializes with fallbackKey and persists ciphertext to DataStore preferences.

conditions.description: AndroidKeyStore fails or throws an exception during encryption.

execution.attacker_perspective: Local adversary or backup inspector inspecting stored preferences.
instructions: Derive AES key using known formula (it * 31 + 17) and decrypt with standard AES-GCM.
execution.observed_result: Plaintext GitHub OAuth token is recovered without AndroidKeyStore hardware-backed protection.

remediation.strategy: Limit fallback key strictly to JVM unit test environments (e.g. check BuildConfig.DEBUG or unit test flags), and fail closed in production if AndroidKeyStore fails.

likelihood.reason: Requires AndroidKeyStore failure or specific JVM environment misconfiguration.

impact.reason: Loss of OAuth token confidentiality allowing repository access.

confidence.reason: Static code analysis reveals hardcoded byte array key in TokenEncryptor.kt.
